findings.title: Explicit manual authorization checksum is ignored when its file is absent
findings.trigger: Run workflow_dispatch with an explicit authorization_sha256 and reviewed base on a narrow change whose checkout has no verification/audit-evidence/release-closeout/authorization.json.
findings.actual: buildCiPlan validates expectedChecksum only inside existsSync(file). With no file it ignores both a malformed explicit value and a syntactically valid but unmatched SHA, then returns a selected plan.
findings.impact: The maintainer-requested validation silently disappears and a manual check can pass without validating the stated approval. This is not an authorized-full or release-publication bypass: broad changes still require source-bound approval, and releasePreflight separately requires the file.
findings.proof: Actual buildCiPlan in an isolated committed Git fixture returned mode=selected for no checksum, HARNESS_AUTHORIZATION_SHA=not-a-hash, and an explicit 64-zero checksum, with identical exact selected test file. No tests or network requests were invoked by the probe.
findings.recommendation: When explicit HARNESS_AUTHORIZATION_SHA is nonempty, require and validate its exact authorization file regardless of the selected change scope. Keep HARNESS_PR_AUTHORIZATION_SHA optional for ordinary targeted PRs lacking a release authorization; do not regress trusted-main handling. Add actual Git-backed missing-file and malformed-input cases alongside existing stale-checksum/source cases.
findings.probeBoundary: The first one-test fixture was correctly rejected because it selected its entire inventory. The final probe includes unselected native fixture files (never run), establishing a genuinely narrow plan instead of weakening that guard.

method: Independent current-contract review using the authorized full3 semantic baseline for unchanged files, with every scope file hash checked against both full3 and frozen full4. Fully reread all five changed documents/workflow/source/test files and followed CI trust-source inputs, planner authorization admission, exact Git source, selector full-inventory boundary, release preflight/publication and coverage consumers. Baseline reuse is explicit below; this is not a claim that all unchanged test/source bodies were freshly reread.

baseline.use: Prior deployment full-source semantic review and previously revalidated tests; all unchanged except README, which was reread in full.

Prior independent tooling/workflow/test semantic review, excluding core/gateway assigned to the runtime auditor this round. All file hashes revalidated; changed files and direct consumer contracts reread here.

focusedReread.purpose: Actual source mapping, full-inventory guard, exact Git changes and CLI prerequisite contract; remaining runner portions use unchanged full3 semantic baseline.
README ancestor-skill scope repair against exact nearest non-symlink .git boundary, descriptor containment and protected roots.

observations: All 193 scoped file hashes match frozen full4. Exactly five differ from full3: affected workflow, deployment README, release preflight lessons, CI planner and its test file. No removal or unreviewed new scope file.

FULL3-DEPLOY-01 documentation now includes precise ancestor .agents/skills roots through the nearest verified Git worktree and retains no-follow/protected-root restrictions; no deployment implementation changed.

Main pushes ignore prior PR variable as intended. PR source cannot authenticate its own full approval; external PR checksums bind exact bytes and source. Manual explicit checksums are enforced when the file exists but miss the no-file branch described above.
The new CI test fixture executes real buildCiPlan for main/manual/PR rather than only selectCiPlan; coverage still omits absent explicit authorization, which the isolated audit probe exposes.

Release preflight independently verifies committed source, exact authorization, pins and build bytes. Publication still requires successful reviewed/security main-push checks for the exact tagged commit and re-resolves the live tag before a single POST.

Root fixture workflow remains hosted-only, builds as ordinary runner, copies exact tracked source and artifacts into its own root-owned temporary checkout, clears inherited environment and requires per-platform case reconciliation. Failed or missing upstream jobs remain failures.

Unchanged deployment contracts retain exact provider/profile byte budgets, generation/official-hash toolchain binding, root/native authorization separation, stopped-service migration, WNOWAIT child identity, unknown-outcome retention, independent history copies, and workspace revision/ownership boundaries from the full3 baseline; current changes do not alter their callers or formats.
limitations: Source/fixture review plus one isolated planner probe, not a full or targeted-suite run.
No production commands, live GitHub calls, external models/MCP, credentials, deployments or source edits.
Actual hosted CI, real systemd boot/TLS issuance and deployed provider access remain separate acceptance work; no fresh claim is made from unchanged fixtures.
One actionable CI input-validation finding remains; this round is not clean.
